name: Subtle laxity (bying ba phra mo)
description: Laxity in which the object remains with some clarity but the intensity of clarity has slackened; the most insidious obstacle to calm abiding because it is mistaken for good meditation.
antidotes: introspective alertness; uplifting the mind (e.g. by recalling the value of the human life)

equivalents.note: the general Buddhist sinking; subtle laxity is its hardest-to-detect form

name: Attachment to this life
description: Concern with the eight worldly concerns of this life, which makes even ethics, study and meditation non-dharma.

equivalents.note: the eight concerns are its content

name: Attachment to saṃsāra (the three realms)
description: Wishing for the happiness of any rebirth in saṃsāra, which prevents renunciation.
antidotes: contemplating the sufferings of saṃsāra and karma

name: Grasping at extremes
description: Grasping at existence, non-existence, both or neither — even at emptiness — which is the absence of the view.
antidotes: resting in the view free of extremes

equivalents.note: grasping emptiness as a view is one form of it

name: Attachment (chags pa)
description: Attachment to anything, which prevents even a good rebirth and cuts the life of liberation.
antidotes: seeing objects of attachment as illusions

name: Meditation as mere absence of thought
description: Resting in a thought-free blankness mistaken for realisation; Sakya Paṇḍita says a fool's Mahāmudrā of this kind leads to animal rebirth, the formless realm or the śrāvaka cessation; the Gelug holds that without analysis it cannot become insight.
antidotes: the wisdom born of empowerment and the two stages (Sakya)

equivalents.note: Kamalaśīla's critique of mere non-thought, on which both draw

name: Hoping for attainments
description: The mind that hopes and asks for accomplishments, removed by knowing that they arise within oneself through dependent arising.

name: Obstacles on the method and wisdom sides (Lamdre)
description: The Vajra Verses list obstacles for the yogin of the method side (guarded against by faith, the protection wheel, mantra and the understanding of phenomena as mind's appearance) and of the wisdom side (outer and inner demon-paths, wrong views, failure to understand the signs, loss of the drop).
antidotes: not separating from the meaning of reality

name: The eight worldly concerns
description: Gain and loss, pleasure and pain, praise and blame, fame and disrepute: practice stained by them is not dharma (Eight Verses 8; Parting 1).

name: Self-cherishing
description: Holding oneself dearer than others; the one into which all blame is driven, the door to all misfortune.

name: The five faults of calm abiding
description: Laziness, forgetting the instruction, laxity and excitement, non-application and over-application.

name: Laxity and excitement
description: The two main obstacles to calm abiding; laxity slackens the hold or clarity, excitement scatters the mind toward desirable objects.

name: Wrongly viewing emptiness
description: Disparaging conventional cause and effect in the name of emptiness (Atiśa); negating too much so that nothing can be posited (Tsongkhapa).

name: The two obscurations
description: Afflictive obscurations and obscurations to knowledge, exhausted only by the perfection of wisdom joined with method.

name: Grasping at inherent existence (true-grasping)
description: The innate apprehension of persons and phenomena as inherently existent — the root of saṃsāra; for Prāsaṅgika even grasping at the self of phenomena is an affliction.
